### Evidence Dossier

#### 1. Feminist Structure Signal

* **Proposed Section:** `feminist_structure_signal`
* **Original Title:** The Photographic Exhibition 'The Women Who Nourish the World' Launches at FAO MuNe FoodS Lab
* **Proposed Chinese Title:** 联合国粮农组织与加拿大国际事务部推出《滋养世界的女性》摄影展：以 11 位女性农人的生命史呈现关护与农业劳动
* **Exact Source URL:** `https://www.fao.org/iywf-2026/events/detail/the-women-who-nourish-the-world-photo-exhibition/en`
* **Image URL:** `https://www.fao.org/media/images/deviywflibraries/default-album/screenshot-2026-10-16-145110.png?sfvrsn=89b25222_1`
* **Primary Entity:** Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) / UPA Développement international / Global Affairs Canada
* **Date:** October 20, 2026
* **Verified Facts:**
  * On October 20, 2026, the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) launched the photographic exhibition *The Women Who Nourish the World* at the FAO MuNe FoodS Lab in Rome, alongside the 54th Session of the Committee on World Food Security (CFS 54).
  * Co-organized by UPA Développement international, Global Affairs Canada, the Québec Delegation in Rome, and the FAO Food and Agriculture Museum and Network, the exhibition marks the International Year of the Woman Farmer 2026.
  * The exhibition features portraits and oral history testimonies of 11 rural women farmers from Benin, Canada, Guinea, Lebanon, and Tunisia.
  * The project centers on women's unpaid and essential labor in agriculture, climate adaptation, food sovereignty, and community care, offering a visual counter-narrative to abstract policy discussions.
* **Why it matters to Muki:** This project brings visibility to marginalized agricultural and care labor. For feminist visual research, it provides a primary case study of how international archives and visual portraiture can center everyday reproductive labor and bodily resilience.
* **Duplication Assessment:** `New` — Neither FAO nor this exhibition has appeared in recent issues.

#### 2. Visual Culture Signal

* **Proposed Section:** `visual_culture_signal`
* **Original Title:** Columbus Museum of Art Opens 'Queer Constellations: Photographs from the Aronowitz Family Collection'
* **Proposed Chinese Title:** 哥伦布艺术博物馆开幕《Queer Constellations》摄影展：通过 50 幅捐赠作品重构酷儿肖像与社区档案
* **Exact Source URL:** `https://www.thelantern.com/2026/10/columbus-museum-of-art-to-open-queer-constellations-photography-exhibit-friday/`
* **Image URL:** `null`
* **Primary Entity:** Columbus Museum of Art (CMA)
* **Date:** October 15, 2026 (News coverage) / Opened mid-October 2026
* **Verified Facts:**
  * The Columbus Museum of Art (CMA) opened *Queer Constellations: Photographs from the Aronowitz Family Collection*, on view through March 21, 2027.
  * Co-curated by Kaitlin Booher, Associate Curator of Photography, the exhibition celebrates a gift of 50 photographic works donated to the museum by the local Aronowitz family.
  * The exhibition focuses on photographic self-representation, domestic intimacy, intergenerational queer histories, and lens-based visual communication.
  * Admission is free for visitors aged 25 and under to foster engagement with student and youth audiences accustomed to image-based communication.
* **Why it matters to Muki:** Shows how private family collections transform into public museum archives. It provides a useful case study in curating queer portraiture and intimate lens-based archives.
* **Duplication Assessment:** `New` — Columbus Museum of Art and this exhibition have not been featured in recent issues.

#### 3. China / East Asia Signal

* **Proposed Section:** `china_east_asia_signal`
* **Original Title:** EyePort 2026 Reverses Roles for Young Photographers' Showcase at Gyeonggi Photography Center
* **Proposed Chinese Title:** 韩国京畿摄影中心举办首届 EyePort 2026：颠覆传统评审模式，由 30 位青年摄影师设展接纳策展人质询
* **Exact Source URL:** `https://www.chosun.com/culture-life/culture/2026/10/21/5J6D5O6N45BNRLLX6R2F5I2RNE/`
* **Image URL:** `null`
* **Primary Entity:** Gyeonggi Photography Center (경기사진센터) / Chosun Ilbo
* **Date:** October 20–21, 2026 (Reported outcome and review) / Event held October 9–10, 2026
* **Verified Facts:**
  * The Gyeonggi Photography Center in Suwon, South Korea, held the inaugural *EyePort 2026* showcase, featuring 30 young photographers under 39 nominated by 15 domestic photography and art experts.
  * The initiative inverted the standard portfolio review power dynamics: instead of artists queuing to pitch to critics, artists established their own booths with prints and photobooks, and visiting curators and critics engaged with them.
  * Artists delivered 5-minute PechaKucha presentations (20 seconds per slide), followed by open dialogue.
  * Seven photographers were selected for long-term institutional support: Kim Do-yeong, Kim Young-kyung, Kim Jae-yeon, Ryu Jun-yeol, Lee Ye-eun, Lee Ha-neul, and Jeong Young-ho.
  * Featured works explored darkroom experimentation, body warmth, depopulation, and spatial digital archives (e.g., Lee Ye-eun's *Raising Indoor Temperature* depicting a body embracing a frozen building exterior).
* **Why it matters to Muki:** Provides an institutional experiment in East Asia that directly challenges curatorial authority and portfolio review mechanics, offering new insights into youth photography ecology and photobook display in South Korea.
* **Duplication Assessment:** `New` — First time recorded.

#### 4. AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

* **Proposed Section:** `ai_creative_tech_signal`
* **Original Title:** NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt Models Enable High-Parameter Agentic Multimodal Reasoning on Local Workstations
* **Proposed Chinese Title:** NVIDIA 发布 Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 混合专家模型：支持 24GB 显存本地端运行，大幅提升 AI Agent 的图像与文档推理能力
* **Exact Source URL:** `https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-nemotron-3-5-super-vl-powers-specialized-agents-with-multimodal-reasoning/`
* **Image URL:** `null`
* **Primary Entity:** NVIDIA / Hugging Face
* **Date:** October 15–16, 2026 (Release) / October 18–21, 2026 (Ecosystem uptake)
* **Verified Facts:**
  * NVIDIA introduced the Nemotron 3.5 open-weight model family, featuring the flagship 120B Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and two local-first Bolt models.
  * The local-first Bolt 74B-A9B model utilizes 2-bit quantization (NVFP4) on a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, activating 9B parameters at runtime while compressing memory requirements to fit within a 24GB VRAM GPU footprint (e.g., RTX / local workstation).
  * The model is optimized for offline agentic workflows, multi-page document parsing (PDFs, charts, tables), UI screen navigation, code debugging, and local tool execution using frameworks like Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, and vLLM.
  * Weights and training recipes have been open-sourced on Hugging Face and ModelScope.
* **Why it matters to Muki:** Brings multimodal agentic reasoning (document parsing, vision-based UI control) to local 24GB VRAM hardware, reducing dependence on closed cloud APIs for sensitive archival and research workflows.
* **Duplication Assessment:** `New` — Previous tech entries focused on Beam, ComfyUI, and Qwen-Image. Nemotron 3.5 Bolt is new.

#### 5. Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

* **Proposed Section:** `archive_opportunity_signal`
* **Original Title:** The Photographers' Gallery Launches 'Future Of Archives' Open Call on Archival Ownership and Counter-Archives
* **Proposed Chinese Title:** 英国摄影师画廊启动“Future Of Archives”开放征集：设立 200 英镑讲者津贴，探讨档案所有权与反向档案实践
* **Exact Source URL:** `https://phmuseum.com/grants/future-of-archives-open-call`
* **Image URL:** `https://img.phmuseum.com/eyJidWNrZXQiOiJpbWcucGhtdXNldW0uY29tIiwia2V5IjoidXNlcnMvZEJCb2puZC9hd2FyZHMvZHdwNms4ZS9ibG9ja3MvZTdxTzU4Yi1nb3BhbkNJY2JZeXR5cWJJIiwiZWRpdHMiOnsicmVzaXplIjp7ImZpdCI6ImNvdmVyIiwid2lkdGgiOjYwMH0sInJvdGF0ZSI6bnVsbH19`
* **Primary Entity:** The Photographers' Gallery, London
* **Date:** Active October 2026 / Submission Deadline: November 1, 2026
* **Verified Facts:**
  * The Photographers' Gallery in London issued an open call titled *Whose Archive is it Anyway?*, the first part of a three-part symposium series on the future of archives.
  * The call prioritizes real-life archival practice over formal academic papers, seeking presentations on family archives, forgotten histories, institutional ownership, counter-archives, and digital preservation.
  * Anyone aged 18+ working with archives and visual memories is eligible.
  * Selected speakers will receive a £200 fee and present at The Photographers' Gallery on April 16, 2027.
  * Deadline for proposals is November 1, 2026.
* **Why it matters to Muki:** Directly aligns with Muki’s focus on counter-archives, media archaeology, and institutional power. It offers a practical opportunity for independent researchers and artists.
* **Duplication Assessment:** `Follow-up` — The Photographers' Gallery appeared in Issue 083 (2026-10-20) for an exhibition (*Sanlé Sory: Colour Years*). This entry represents a distinct new development: an open call on archival theory and practice.
